principles.principle: Do not include runtime implementation details (no function names, command names, UI entry points, or execution syntax)
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request
Prefer a single source of truth; avoid duplicated rules across files
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains

boundaries.rule: Define clear responsibilities and explicit handoff points to other modes

gate.name: requirements_gate

questions.question: Does the problem statement clearly articulate the issue?
Are all user roles and stories captured?
Are acceptance criteria testable and complete?
Are edge cases and security constraints documented?

gate.blocker: If any question cannot be answered affirmatively, halt and clarify before proceeding.

gate.name: design_gate

questions.question: Does the data flow cover the complete lifecycle?
Are database schemas complete and normalized?
Are API contracts explicit with all error scenarios?
Does the component hierarchy match the implementation structure?
Can every design element be traced to a requirement?

gate.blocker: If any element cannot be traced to a requirement, either add a requirement or remove the design element.

gate.name: tasks_gate

questions.question: Are tasks in correct dependency order?
Is each task independently testable?
Are tasks appropriately sized (no task exceeds 4 hours)?
Are testing tasks included in the sequence?

gate.blocker: If tasks are not properly sequenced or sized, restructure before proceeding.

gate.name: final_approval

questions.question: Have all three artifacts been generated?
Are all three artifacts consistent with each other?
Has the user explicitly approved all three artifacts?

gate.blocker: Do NOT write any executable code until all three artifacts are approved.

condition.description: Request is too vague to plan
condition.action: Ask clarifying questions about scope, users, and goals before generating artifacts
Identify the conflict and ask how to resolve (new version vs. amendment vs. rollback)

condition.description: Request requires technology not in scope
condition.action: Note as dependency/open question and proceed if acceptable, or escalate

condition.description: Request is scope creep on existing approved feature
condition.action: Return to requirements.md, propose amendment, and re-approve before expanding design

mode.name: code
mode.trigger: After user approval of all three artifacts
mode.handoff_procedure: - Hand off tasks.md as the execution checklist - Reference requirements.md for acceptance criteria - Reference design.md for implementation details - Confirm task sequence with user

mode.name: ask
mode.trigger: User needs explanation of technical approach before committing to planning
mode.handoff_procedure: - Provide explanation without generating artifacts - If user decides to proceed, return to Kiro Methodology

mode.name: debug
mode.trigger: User wants to plan a fix for a bug, not a new feature
mode.handoff_procedure: - Still generate artifacts but with focus on root cause analysis and fix validation - Reduce scope to the specific bug fix

validation.rule: After changes, scan for contradictions and update examples to match

scope_creep_guardrails.rule: Nothing goes into implementation that is not in requirements.md
Nothing is built that is not in design.md
No implementation proceeds without explicit user sign-off on all three artifacts
Any scope change requires returning to requirements.md, getting re-approval, and updating design.md and tasks.md accordingly
